evidenceSummary.excerpt: Orion, like a fickle youth, was soon consoled for their disappearance, and loved Merope, daughter of Œnopion, King of Chios, who consented to their union on condition that his future son-in-law should win his bride by some heroic deed.
Blind, helpless, and alone, he now wandered from place to place, hoping to find some one capable of restoring his sight.
"When, blinded by Œnopion, He sought the blacksmith at his forge, And, climbing up the mountain gorge, Fixed his blank eyes upon the sun."
